clue.text: Knocked about a lot, as veteran campaigners?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for someone covered in bruises and scrapes, much injured
old soldiers who have served in many conflicts have literally been through battles

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being battered and bruised literally describes soldiers who have fought in many campaigns.

parts.note: to put someone down in the ground once they are late, meaning dead, is to bury them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down as late' reads like recording someone as tardy; 'the late' also means the dead, who are put down into a grave.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury, putting a deceased person into the ground.

clue.text: He will have marked cards, of course

definitions.text: He will have marked cards, of course

parts.words: He will have marked cards, of course
parts.note: a racing adviser marks his selections on the racecards at a racecourse

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a card cheat; 'course' is a racecourse and the cards are racecards.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing tipster picks likely winners, marking them on the race programme.

clue.text: Departures could be set about eleven

indicators.note: the reordered letters go around the Roman numeral
the word set could be arranged differently, so its letters are reordered

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A timetable showing departures scheduled for around eleven o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'set' as scheduled; it is the anagram fodder, with 'could be' rearranging it and 'about' wrapping the result round the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Exits are departures, ways of leaving or acts of leaving.

clue.text: Guardian supported by American in prayer

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the second, held up by it

parts.note: a guardian angel watches over someone
US is short for American, as in US citizen

explanation.surface: A guardian figure backed by an American takes part in prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angelus is a Catholic devotional prayer recited morning, noon and evening.

clue.text: Rigid line taken by hospital department

indicators.note: the first piece is taken by, and followed by, the second

parts.note: a string is a line or cord
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital department adopts a strict policy line.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringent rules are strict and unbending, so rigid in application.

parts.note: on a boat, a painter is the line used to tie it up, made of cord

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests paint or canvas; a painter is also the mooring line at a boat's bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat's painter is a length of cordage, so that is what it is made from.

indicators.note: a silly arrangement of the letters puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone snaps back that a piece of writing is rubbish and foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick sharp reply, a retort.

clue.text: In favour of moving to get a better job?

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
motion is the act of moving

explanation.surface: Someone backs a change of post in the hope of advancement.
explanation.definitionFit: A promotion is advancement to a higher position at work.

definitions.meaning: coming to a halt, as a car does
a dental filling, an old word for which is a ...

explanation.definitionFit: Halting is coming to a stop, and a stopping is an older name for a tooth filling.

clue.text: Wild parrot, a bird of prey

indicators.note: wild letters are out of control and rearranged

explanation.surface: An untamed parrot turns out to be a hunting bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A raptor is a hawk, eagle or other predatory bird.

clue.text: Grinds away at university course, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Greats is the Oxford degree course in classics

explanation.surface: A student slaves away at a demanding degree course.
explanation.walkthrough: GREATS is the name of the classics degree at Oxford University.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that grates grinds or rasps against a surface.

definitions.meaning: an outsider with little hope of success
a marksman firing from great distance takes a far shot

explanation.definitionFit: A long shot is an unlikely bet, and literally a shot from a long way off.

clue.text: Ancient city's role in South Africa

indicators.note: the role goes inside the country's abbreviation

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek city is said to play a part in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was a powerful city-state of ancient Greece.

indicators.note: re-collected means gathered together again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A stroll remembered in a poem set in the Forest of Arden.
explanation.definitionFit: A promenade is a leisurely walk, or a place for one.

indicators.note: various suggests the letters are mixed in diverse ways

explanation.surface: Reporting from many regions keeps people informed.
explanation.definitionFit: Awareness is knowledge or consciousness of something.

parts.note: read as a phrase, to ... is to give up sin, which a malicious woman would never do

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as SHED EVIL, 'abandon wickedness': the clue says the woman it names would never do so.
explanation.definitionFit: A she-devil is a cruel, spiteful woman.

clue.text: Clock at one perhaps? Have a drink

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be put another way

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Seeing the clock at one o'clock prompts someone to go for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges CLOCK, AT and I together.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail is a mixed alcoholic drink.

clue.text: We hear officers are at the heart of things

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: colonels are senior army officers

explanation.surface: Senior army officers are said to be at the centre of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Kernels are the central or essential parts of things, their cores.

parts.note: one who lurches is staggering, and a four-legged dog of this breed walks on all fours

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a drunk crawling; the answer is a dog breed whose name looks like 'one who lurches'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lurcher is a crossbred dog, typically part greyhound, and literally one who lurches.

clue.text: Gift for producing story book in abbreviated form

parts.note: a tale is a story
NT is the abbreviation for the New Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A gift for writing stories, published in shortened form.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a natural gift or aptitude.

clue.text: Good characters are, for example, caught in wicked libel

indicators.note: the abbreviation is caught inside the rearranged letters
wicked suggests the letters are twisted out of shape

explanation.surface: Good people are, for example, ensnared in a malicious libel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' rearranges the clue's libel as LIBLE and 'caught in' places the abbreviation after its first letter; the definition is a whole phrase, describing what good characters are.
explanation.definitionFit: Good handwritten letters are clear and readable, so the characters are said to be easy to read.

indicators.note: repeatedly means the word is given twice

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court

explanation.surface: Keep trying to show you agree.
explanation.definitionFit: Hear hear is the cry of agreement heard in Parliament and at meetings.

indicators.note: disturbed letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A hunting dog upsets an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The dugong is a large marine mammal, a sea cow.

parts.note: a river's current issues into the sea at the coast through spreading mouths

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a topical seaside problem; 'issue' means an outflow, where a river meets the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A delta is the fan of channels formed where a river flows out into the sea.

indicators.note: sound tells us to say the word aloud

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing or no

explanation.surface: Edits made silently to a recording.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicks are small cuts or notches.

clue.text: Staff, say, joining English riding school

parts.note: to staff is to man, to provide with workers
say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: Employees join an English school for horse riding.
explanation.definitionFit: A manege is an arena or school for training horses and riders.

parts.note: a graduate is a BA, two letters which are half of the four-letter word back

explanation.walkthrough: BA, a Bachelor of Arts, is literally half of the word BACK; a half back is also a midfield footballing position.
explanation.definitionFit: A halfback is a player positioned between the forwards and the defenders.

definitions.meaning: golf balls are perched on little pegs before driving

explanation.definitionFit: Golf tees are little pegs holding up the ball, and the Tees flows through north-east England.

indicators.note: the vessels carry the letter inside them

parts.note: steamers are steam-powered ships

explanation.surface: Vessels flying flags to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Streamers are long narrow flags or ribbons, like pennants.
